newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds sell off on rate fears, dollar dips vs. yen.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds sell off on rate fears, dollar dips vs. yen.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks plunged Wednesday as long-term bond interest rates rose amid fresh fears that the economy's strong growth would prompt an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
The dollar fell to its lowest level in a month against the Japanese yen after a news report said Japan, the United States and Germany were planning to sell dollars for yen.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 139.67 points, or 1.93 percent, to close at 7,085.65, backing off from Tuesday's record finish of 7,225.32.

It was the Dow's steepest plunge since April 11 and erased most of the 154 points it had gained during back-to-back record-setting sessions in the two prior days, including a 143-point rise on Monday.
In the broader market, declining issues outnumbered advances 1,657 to 845 on active volume of 497 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index lost 5.39 points to 1,322.91.
With the majority of corporate earnings already reported for the quarter, investors had little choice but to focus on the bond market.
"When there are no earnings to move the market, the stock market and bond market move in tandem," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 29/32 point, or $9.06 per $1,000 face value, raising its yield to 6.96 percent from 6.89 percent on Tuesday, after a disappointing auction of 10-year Treasury notes. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
With attention again focused on interest rates, analysts said the market's next turn could quickly put the latest rally to the test.

"Certainly if rates keep rising and volatility keeps going along the way it has, that's going to give investors cause to pause and think about what it is they're doing," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates.
The dollar has risen 10 percent so far this year against the yen, reaching a 56-month high of 127.47 yen on May 1.
The dollar closed at 124.97 yen, down from 125.38 at Tuesday's close, and 1.7191 German marks, down from 1.7245, while the British pound slid to $1.6135 from $1.6332.

Soybean prices rose on rumours of buying interest from China and a cut in Brazil's estimated soybean production by a U.S. government official. At the Chicago Board of Trade, soybeans for May delivery closed 2 cents a bushel higher at $8.96 after posting a new life-of-contract high at $9.03-1/2.

Wheat prices also rose as export demand picked up and concerns about freeze damage to the U.S. winter wheat crop resurfaced on reports from crop tours. Wheat for May delivery closed 1 cent a bushel higher at $3.95 after rising as high as $4.02 during the session.

At the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, pork belly futures shot up for strong gains after a report showed extremely heavy movement of bellies out of cold storage. Pork bellies for delivery in May ended 2.05 cents a pound up at 89.85 cents.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 still managed to end 18.2 points firmer to a record closing level of 4,537.5. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average fell 132.02 points to 20,048.90.
